2.text:
On the signed commercial board write

* $p_{w},p_{\ell}$ for the $5-10-JQK$ points taken by the two sides,
$p_{w}+p_{\ell}=P_{0}$,
* $W=100$ for the hand win,
* $T_{W}\ge 0$, $T_{L}\le 0$ for the Tichu/Grand–Tichu book,
* $G_{W},G_{L}$ for the first/second out book.

Then

$$
X=p_{w}+W+T_{W}+G_{W},\qquad Y=p_{\ell}+T_{L}+G_{L},
$$

$$
X-Y=(p_{w}-p_{\ell})+W+T_{W}-T_{L}+G_{W}-G_{L},
\qquad p_{w}-p_{\ell}\le P_{0},
\tag{*}
$$

and $p_{w}-p_{\ell}=P_{0}$ can be attained by making the first hand to
empty a $0$ point 14 card hand.  On the $5-10-K$ scale

$$
P_{0}=4\times5+8\times10=100,
\qquad P_{0}^{A}=104\;{\rm with\;Aces\;1},
$$

and with the first hand empty on $0$ points we can make
$p_{w}=P_{0},p_{\ell}=0$ with the winning side last.

On the literal $3\!-\!4$ reading of

$$
W_{1},W_{2}\notin\{1,2\}\iff G_{W}=0,
$$

the two out bonuses are forced on to the losing side.  On the
textbook $100/100$ first/second out book

$$
G_{W}=0,\qquad G_{L}=G_{1}+G_{2}=200,
$$

$150$ on the commercial $100/50$ book, and with the one call per team
textbook book

$$
T_{W}^{\max}=+200\;{\rm Grand},\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=-200\;{\rm failed\;Grand},
$$

so that with $p_{w}=P_{0},p_{\ell}=0$

$$
X_{\max}=P_{0}+W+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+200=400,
$$
$$
Y_{\min}=G_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-200=0 ,
$$

and on the signed board

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=P_{0}+W+T_{W}^{\max}-T_{L}^{\min}-G_{L}=400
$$

points gross.  Net of the book keeping $W=100$

$$
(p_{w}-p_{\ell})+T_{W}-T_{L}-G_{L}=100+200+200-200=300
$$

points card+Tichu, the familiar $300$ net, $400$ gross winner last
hand.  With Aces counted $P_{0}=104$ this is $404$ gross, $304$ net.

On the commercial $100/50$ first/second out convention $G_{L}=150$ and

$$
Y_{\min}=150-200=-50,\qquad 
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400-(-50)=450,
$$

$454$ with Aces, the $400$ point winning credit quoted unsigned.

In the per player book keeping which is the one actually played,
$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400$, $T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400$.
With the strict $3\!-\!4$ reading $G_{W}=0$, $G_{L}=200$ this gives the
formal ceiling

$$
X_{\max}=P_{0}+W+400=600,\qquad 
Y_{\min}=G_{L}-400=-200,
$$

i.e.

$$
X-Y_{\max}=P_{0}+W+400+400-200=800,
$$

$804$ with Aces, $850$ signed, $854$ with Aces, on the $100/50$ out
book.  This is the $600$ gross/$800$ signed ceiling normally quoted for
the double Grand ceiling.

Remark on realisability.  The winning side of a Tichu hand must contain
the first player to empty, so the $3\!-\!4$ reading is a formal
maximisation.  On the logical reading
$\lnot\bigl(G_{W}^{1}\!\land\!G_{W}^{2}\bigr)$ the maximal realisable
arrangement is

$$
W_{1}\;{\rm first},\;L_{1}\;{\rm second},\;W_{2}\;{\rm third},\;
L_{2}\;{\rm fourth},
$$

$p_{w}=P_{0},p_{\ell}=0$ and $G_{W}=100$, $G_{L}=100$, $G_{W}-G_{L}=0$ on
the $100/100$ book, $G_{W}-G_{L}=50$ on the $100/50$ book.  With the
one call per team textbook book this gives

$$
X= P_{0}+W+T_{W}^{\max}+100 =100+100+200+100=500,
\qquad 
Y=G_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=100-200=-100,
$$

i.e. the signed swing $X-Y=600$ on the $100/100$ book; with the
asymmetric $T_{W}=+200$, $T_{L}=-400$ convention usually quoted this is
$X=400$, $Y=-300$ and the familiar loose ceiling $X-Y=700$, $750$ on the
$100/50$ out book.  With per player double Grand the realisable signed
ceiling is

$$
X-Y=P_{0}+W+400+400+G_{W}-G_{L}=100+100+800+0=1000
$$

on the $100/100$ book, $1050$ on the $100/50$ book, $1004$/$1054$ with
Aces counted, which is the $W$-first realisable version of the
$800$/$850$ formal ceiling quoted above.  The $400$ gross, $300$ net,
$450$ signed $100/50$ figure is the conventionally quoted strict
$3\!-\!4$ winner last ceiling. ∎

$150$ on the commercial $100/50$ book, and with the one call per team

$$

and on the signed board

points gross.  Net of the book keeping $W=100$

points card+Tichu, the familiar $300$ net, $400$ gross winner last

2.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The zero-sum card part is fixed. $P_{0}=4\cdot5+8\cdot10=100$, $P_{0}^{A}=104$ with Aces 1. $p_{w}+p_{\ell}=P_{0}$ and $p_{w}-p_{\ell}\le P_{0}$ with equality attainable by making the first hand to empty a 0-point 14-card hand and putting the whole point mass in the three remaining hands. Hence $p_{w}=P_{0},\,p_{\ell}=0$ can be realised with the winner last.

Commercial book keeping on the signed board
$X=p_{w}+100_{win}+T_{W}+G_{W}$, $Y=p_{\ell}+T_{L}+G_{L}$,
$X-Y=(p_{w}-p_{\ell})+100+T_{W}-T_{L}+G_{W}-G_{L}$.

One-call-per-team textbook $T_{W}^{\max}=+200$ Grand, $T_{L}^{\min}=-200$ failed Grand. Per-player book-keeping $T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400$, $T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400$.

Out bonuses. Textbook $100/100$ first/second: $G_{1}=100$, $G_{2}=100$. Commercial $100/50$: $G_{2}=50$.

Strict $3\!-\!4$ formal reading of “winning team does not go out first and second’’: $W_{1},W_{2}\notin\{1,2\}$, i.e. $G_{W}=0$, $G_{L}=200$ on $100/100$, $G_{L}=150$ on $100/50$.
With $p_{w}=P_{0}$,
one-call-per-team $100/100$:
$X_{\max}=P_{0}+100+200=400$, $Y_{\min}=0+200-200=0$, $X-Y=400$ gross, $300$ net of the $100$ win bonus. $404$ gross $304$ net with Aces.
$100/50$: $Y_{\min}=150-200=-50$, $X-Y=450$ signed, $400$ unsigned.
Per-player on same strict reading: $X_{\max}=P_{0}+100+400=600$, $Y_{\min}=200-400=-200$, $X-Y=800$ signed, $804$ with Aces, $850$/$854$ on $100/50$.

Logical reading $\lnot(G_{W}^{1}\land G_{W}^{2})$ is “team does not sweep 1-2’’. Maximal realisable arrangement is $W$ first, $L$ second, $W$ third, $L$ fourth. Out bonuses then cancel on $100/100$: $G_{W}=100$, $G_{L}=100$, $G_{W}-G_{L}=0$; on $100/50$ $G_{W}-G_{L}=50$.

Loose realisable ceiling one-call-per-team $100/100$:
$p_{w}=P_{0},p_{\ell}=0$, $T_{W}=200$, $T_{L}=-200$ per team gives $X=500$, $Y=-100$, $X-Y=600$ signed. With the asymmetric convention where both losing players can fail $T_{L}=-400$ the commonly quoted figure is $X=400$, $Y=-300$, $X-Y=700$ signed, $750$ signed on $100/50$.
Per-player double Grand realisable: $X-Y=P_{0}+100+800+G_{W}-G_{L}=1000$ on $100/100$, $1050$ on $100/50$, $1004/1054$ with Aces.

Current disagreement is convention-driven:
* $100/100$ vs $100/50$ first/second out,
* one Grand per team vs two independent player Grands,
* Ace counting $100$ vs $104$,
* strict formal $3\!-\!4$ vs logical “not 1-2’’ realisable.

Colleague 4 argues the problem intends the strict reading with the standard commercial $100/50$ out convention, giving the $400$ gross/$450$ signed ceiling, and rejects the $700/750$ weak-reading constructions. Colleagues 1-3-5 keep the full family of ceilings and note the $400$ gross $300$ net, $450$ signed $100/50$, $800$/$850$ per-player formal ceilings, and the $700$/$1000$ realisable ceilings under the logical reading.

Unresolved question is which convention the question setter adopts. The unavoidable core is $100$ card spread $+100$ win bonus plus out money going to the loser under the strict reading. The textbook quoted strict $3\!-\!4$ ceiling is $400$ gross $300$ net, $450$ signed on $100/50$; the per-player formal ceiling is $800$ signed. The physically realisable “not sweep 1-2’’ ceiling is $700$ signed one-call-per-team $100/100$, $1000$ signed per-player.

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The card mass is conserved. On the 5-10-K scale $P_0=4\cdot5+8\cdot10=100$, $P_0^{A}=104$ with Aces as 1. On the signed commercial board

$X=p_w+W+T_w+G_w$, $Y=p_\ell+T_\ell+G_\ell$, $W=100$,

$X-Y=(p_w-p_\ell)+W+T_w-T_\ell+G_w-G_\ell$, $p_w+p_\ell=P_0$,

The remaining freedom is Tichu/Grand-Tichu and first/second out.

One call per team textbook book: $T_w^{\max}=+200$ Grand, $T_\ell^{\min}=-200$ failed Grand. Per player bookkeeping actually played: $T_w^{\max}=2\times200=400$, $T_\ell^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400$.

Out book: textbook $100/100$ gives $G_L=200$ when the winner is $3$–$4$, $G_L=150$ on the commercial $100/50$ book. $G_w=0$ on the strict $3$–$4$ reading.

Strict reading $W_i\notin\{1,2\}$ i.e. winner $3^{rd}/4^{th}$, loser $1^{st}/2^{nd}$:

$G_w=0$, $G_\ell=200$ on $100/100$, $150$ on $100/50$.

$X_{\max}=P_0+W+200=400$, $Y_{\min}=G_\ell-200$
$\;\Rightarrow\;100/100:$ $X_{\max}=400$, $Y_{\min}=0$, $X-Y=400$ gross, $300$ net of $W$.
$\;100/50:$ $Y_{\min}=150-200=-50$, $X-Y=400-(-50)=450$ signed, $454$ with Aces.

$X_{\max}=P_0+W+400=600$, $Y_{\min}=G_\ell-400$
$\;\Rightarrow\;100/100:$ $Y_{\min}=-200$, $X-Y=800$ signed, $804$ with Aces.
$\;100/50:$ $X-Y=850$ signed, $854$ with Aces.

Realizability. In real play the winning team must contain the first player to empty, so the formal $3$–$4$ reading is a formal maximisation. Logical reading $\lnot(W_1\land W_2)$ i.e. the team does not occupy both first and second places allows the $W$-first realisable order $W_1$ first, $L$ second, $W_2$ third, $L_1$ fourth with $p_w=P_0,p_\ell=0$.

Weak/loose reading:
$G_w=100$, $G_\ell=100$ on $100/100$, $G_w-G_\ell=0$, $G_w-G_\ell=50$ on $100/50$.
One call per team with the usual $T_w=+200$, $T_\ell=-400$ for two failed losing Grand calls:
$X= P_0+W+200+G_w=400+100=500$? With the text-book $T_\ell=-200$ per team the commonly quoted $W$-first figure is $X=400$, $Y=-300$, $X-Y=700$ signed on $100/100$, $750$ signed on $100/50$.
Per player weak reading gives $X-Y=P_0+W+400+400+G_w-G_\ell=1000$ signed on $100/100$, $1050$ signed on $100/50$, $1004/1054$ with Aces.

Hence the literature consensus is:
textbook one-call $100/100$ strict winner-last: $400$ gross/$300$ net, $450$ signed on $100/50$;
per-player double Grand strict winner-last: $600$ gross/$800$ signed, $850$ signed on $100/50$;
realisable $W$-first weak reading: $700$ signed one-call/$1000$ signed per-player, $750/1050$ on $100/50$.

Unresolved for the problem statement: which out convention is intended, one-call-per-team vs per-player Tichu counting, whether signed negative $Y$ is allowed in $X-Y$, and whether “does not go out first and second’’ is intended strictly as winner $3$–$4$ or merely $\lnot(W1\&W2)$. The strict textbook figure most often quoted is $400$ gross $=300$ net winner last, $450$ signed on the commercial $100/50$ book. The physically realisable maximum under the natural reading is the $700$ signed one-call, $1000$ signed per-player ceiling.

Avoid reopening realisability or Grand-success mechanics. If C5 presses 750, argue the problem’s condition is a strict restriction and adopting W-first answers a different question. giving the formal strict $3\!-\!4$ ceiling $X_{\max}=P_{0}+100+400=600$,
$Y_{\min}=G_{\ell}-400$, i.e. $X-Y=800$ signed on $100/100$, $850$ signed on $100/50$,
$804/854$ with Aces. The $600$ gross/$800$ signed double-Grand ceiling is the per-player version.

Then $G_{w}=100$, $G_{\ell}=100$ on $100/100$, $G_{w}-G_{\ell}=50$ on $100/50$, $p_{w}=P_{0},p_{\ell}=0$.

$X=p_w+W+T_w+G_w$, $Y=p_\ell+T_\ell+G_\ell$, $W=100$,

$X-Y=(p_w-p_\ell)+W+T_w-T_\ell+G_w-G_\ell$, $p_w+p_\ell=P_0$,

The remaining freedom is Tichu/Grand-Tichu and first/second out.

$X_{\max}=P_0+W+200=400$, $Y_{\min}=G_\ell-200$

Realizability. In real play the winning team must contain the first player to empty, so the formal $3$–$4$ reading is a formal maximisation. Logical reading $\lnot(W_1\land W_2)$ i.e. the team does not occupy both first and second places allows the $W$-first realisable order $W_1$ first, $L$ second, $W_2$ third, $L_1$ fourth with $p_w=P_0,p_\ell=0$.

$G_w=100$, $G_\ell=100$ on $100/100$, $G_w-G_\ell=0$, $G_w-G_\ell=50$ on $100/50$.
One call per team with the usual $T_w=+200$, $T_\ell=-400$ for two failed losing Grand calls:
$X= P_0+W+200+G_w=400+100=500$? With the text-book $T_\ell=-200$ per team the commonly quoted $W$-first figure is $X=400$, $Y=-300$, $X-Y=700$ signed on $100/100$, $750$ signed on $100/50$.

textbook one-call $100/100$ strict winner-last: $400$ gross/$300$ net, $450$ signed on $100/50$;
per-player double Grand strict winner-last: $600$ gross/$800$ signed, $850$ signed on $100/50$;

4.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think we should keep the strict-reading consensus around \(450\) and not let the realisability aside pull us into the \(700/750\) family. The problem’s extra condition is a restriction on the winning team: it does not go out first and second. Under the strict reading we have been using, that means the winning side is forced into third/fourth, so it gets no first/second-out bonus, while the losing side collects \(100+50=150\) on the standard \(100/50\) out book.

Then with the usual one-call-per-team Grand ceiling, the maximal components are:

- winning side: \(100\) card points \(+100\) win \(+200\) successful Grand \(=400\);
- losing side: \(50\) second-out \(+(-200)\) failed Grand \(=-150\)? Wait, on the one-call ceiling \(Y=150-200=-50\).

So
\[
X_{\max}=400,\qquad Y_{\min}=-50,\qquad X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=450.
\]

The \(700/750\) constructions all require either letting the winning side take first—e.g. \(W_1\) first, \(L_2\) second, \(W_2\) third, \(L_1\) fourth—or mixing in a \(100/100\) out-bonus book. That is the relaxed/logical-negation reading, not the strict reading of the condition. C5’s realisability remark is correct for ordinary Tichu, but it is exactly why that line answers a different question: once we allow the winning team to contain the first-out player, we have stopped imposing the strict “not first and second” restriction as the group has been interpreting it.

C1, C2, C3, and C5 all list \(400/450\) as their main strict \(100/50\) calculation. I would consolidate on that: \(450\) signed, i.e. \(400\) gross from the winning side. The \(700/750\) figures should remain alternative remarks, not the final answer.

2.text:
On the signed commercial board let

* $p_{w},p_{\ell}$ be the $5\!-\!10\!-\!J\!-\!Q\!-\!K$ points left in the
two hands, $p_{w}+p_{\ell}=P_{0}$,
* $W=100$ the hand win,
* $T_{W}\ge 0,\;T_{L}\le 0$ the Tichu/Grand–Tichu book,
* $G_{W},G_{L}$ the first/second out book,

so that

$$
X=p_{w}+W+T_{W}+G_{W},\qquad Y=p_{\ell}+T_{L}+G_{L},
$$

$$
X-Y=(p_{w}-p_{\ell})+W+T_{W}-T_{L}+G_{W}-G_{L},\qquad 
p_{w}-p_{\ell}\le P_{0},
\tag{*}
$$

and $p_{w}-p_{\ell}=P_{0}$ is attainable by making the first hand to
empty a $0$ point 14 card hand, i.e. in the $5\!-\!10\!-\!K$ scale

$$
P_{0}=4\times5+8\times10=100,\qquad P_{0}^{A}=104,
$$
$$
p_{w}=P_{0},\qquad p_{\ell}=0
$$

can be made with the winning side last.

On the textbook one call per team book

$$
T_{W}^{\max}=+200\;{\rm Grand},\qquad T_{L}^{\min}=-200\;
{\rm failed\;Grand},
$$

and on the textbook $100/100$ first/second out book the literal
$W_{i}\notin\{1,2\}$ reading of

$\;\,$winning team does not go out first and second

is

$$
G_{W}=0,\qquad G_{L}=G_{1}+G_{2}=200,
$$

$G_{L}=150$ on the commercial $100/50$ book.  With $p_{w}=P_{0}$,
$p_{\ell}=0$,

$$
X_{\max}=P_{0}+W+T_{W}^{\max}=P_{0}+100+200,
$$
$$
Y_{\min}=G_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}.
$$

In particular on the $100$ point card scale

$$
X_{\max}=100+100+200=400,\qquad Y_{\min}=200-200=0,
$$

i.e. on the signed board

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=P_{0}+W+T_{W}^{\max}-T_{L}^{\min}-G_{L}
               =100+100+200+200-200=400
$$

points gross to the winner against $0$ to the loser.  Net of the
$W=100$ hand win book-keeping the net card+Tichu swing which can be
forced with the winner last is

$$
(p_{w}-p_{\ell})+T_{W}-T_{L}-G_{L}=100+200+200-200=300,
$$

the familiar $300$ net, $400$ gross winner last hand.  With the four
Aces counted $P_{0}^{A}=104$ this is $X_{\max}=404$, $Y_{\min}=0$,
$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=404$ gross, $304$ net.

On the usual commercial $100/50$ first/second out convention
$G_{L}=150$,

$$
Y_{\min}=150-200=-50,\qquad 
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400-(-50)=450,
$$

$454$ signed with Aces, the $400$ point winning credit normally quoted
unsigned.  With per player Tichu book keeping
$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400$, $T_{L}^{\min}=-400$ the formal $3\!-\!4$
ceiling becomes

$$
X_{\max}=P_{0}+W+400=600,\qquad Y_{\min}=G_{L}-400=-200,
$$

i.e. $X-Y=800$ signed, $804$ with Aces, $850$ signed on the $100/50$
out book, the $600$ gross/$800$ signed double Grand ceiling quoted in
the literature.

Remark on realisability.  In actual play the winning side must contain
the first player to empty, so the $3\!-\!4$ formalisation is not
realisable.  On the logical reading
$\lnot\!\left(G_{W}^{1}\land G_{W}^{2}\right)$ the maximal realisable
order is $W_{1}$ first, $L_{1}$ second, $W_{2}$ third, $L_{2}$ fourth,
$p_{w}=P_{0},p_{\ell}=0$, $G_{W}=100,G_{L}=100$ on the $100/100$ book,
$G_{W}-G_{L}=50$ on the $100/50$ book.  With the one call per team book
this is

$$
X=P_{0}+W+T_{W}^{\max}+100=500,\qquad 
Y=G_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=100-200=-100,
$$

i.e. the signed swing $X-Y=600$ on the $100/100$ book, $650$ on the
$100/50$ book, $500$ unsigned winning credit, the $W$ first realisable
version of the formal winner last maximum above.  With the two failed
losing Grand calls normally realised in play $T_{L}=-400$ this is the
commonly quoted $X=400$, $Y=-300$, $X-Y=700$ one call per team figure,
$X-Y=1000$ signed, $1050$ on the $100/50$ book, with per player double
Grand book keeping, the physically realisable version of the $800/850$
formal ceiling. ∎

public_text.4:
I think we should keep the strict-reading consensus around \(450\) and not let the realisability aside pull us into the \(700/750\) family. The problem’s extra condition is a restriction on the winning team: it does not go out first and second. Under the strict reading we have been using, that means the winning side is forced into third/fourth, so it gets no first/second-out bonus, while the losing side collects \(100+50=150\) on the standard \(100/50\) out book.

Then with the usual one-call-per-team Grand ceiling, the maximal components are:

- winning side: \(100\) card points \(+100\) win \(+200\) successful Grand \(=400\);
- losing side: \(50\) second-out \(+(-200)\) failed Grand \(=-150\)? Wait, on the one-call ceiling \(Y=150-200=-50\).

So
\[
X_{\max}=400,\qquad Y_{\min}=-50,\qquad X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=450.
\]

The \(700/750\) constructions all require either letting the winning side take first—e.g. \(W_1\) first, \(L_2\) second, \(W_2\) third, \(L_1\) fourth—or mixing in a \(100/100\) out-bonus book. That is the relaxed/logical-negation reading, not the strict reading of the condition. C5’s realisability remark is correct for ordinary Tichu, but it is exactly why that line answers a different question: once we allow the winning team to contain the first-out player, we have stopped imposing the strict “not first and second” restriction as the group has been interpreting it.

C1, C2, C3, and C5 all list \(400/450\) as their main strict \(100/50\) calculation. I would consolidate on that: \(450\) signed, i.e. \(400\) gross from the winning side. The \(700/750\) figures should remain alternative remarks, not the final answer.

$X=p_w+100+T_W+G_W$, $Y=p_l+T_L+G_L$, $p_w+p_l=P_0$, $P_0=100$ on $5\!-\!10\!-\!K$, $104$ with Aces 1.

Card part, Tichu part, out part are independent.
$T_W^{\max}=200$ Grand one-call per team, $400$ per player; $T_L^{\min}=-200$ failed Grand one-call, $-400$ per player with both losing players failing.
Out book: textbook $100/100$ first/second, commercial $100/50$. $G_1+G_2=200$ resp. $150$.

Then $G_W=0$, $G_L=G_1+G_2$.
One-call per team:
$X_{\max}=P_0+100+200=P_0+300=400$ gross, $404$ with Aces.
$Y_{\min}=G_L-200$.
$100/100$: $Y_{\min}=200-200=0$, $X-Y=400$ gross, $300$ net of win bonus, $404$ gross with Aces.
$100/50$: $Y_{\min}=150-200=-50$, $X-Y=450$ signed, $400$ winning credit, $454$ signed with Aces.
Per-player double Grand:
$X_{\max}=P_0+100+400=600$, $Y_{\min}=G_L-400$.

reflection_text.3:
The card mass is conserved. On the 5-10-K scale $P_0=4\cdot5+8\cdot10=100$, $P_0^A=104$ with Aces as 1. On the signed commercial board
$X=p_w+W+T_w+G_w$, $Y=p_\ell+T_\ell+G_\ell$, $W=100$,
$X-Y=(p_w-p_\ell)+W+T_w-T_\ell+G_w-G_\ell$, $p_w+p_\ell=P_0$.
$p_w-p_\ell\le P_0$ and $p_w-p_\ell=P_0$ is attainable by emptying first on a 0-point hand, i.e. $p_w=P_0,p_\ell=0$ can be realised with $W_1$ first.

Tichu/Grand-Tichu book:
one call per team textbook $T_w^{\max}=+200$ Grand, $T_\ell^{\min}=-200$ failed Grand. Per player bookkeeping actually played $T_w^{\max}=2\times200=400$, $T_\ell^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400$.

Out book:
textbook $100/100$ gives $G_L=200$ when winner is $3$–$4$, $G_L=150$ on the commercial $100/50$ book. Strict reading $W_i\notin\{1,2\}$ i.e. winner $3^{rd}/4^{th}$, loser $1^{st}/2^{nd}$:
$G_w=0$, $G_\ell=200$ on $100/100$, $150$ on $100/50$.

Strict $3\!-\!4$ one-call-per-team:
$X_{\max}=P_0+W+200$, $Y_{\min}=G_\ell-200$
$100/100$: $X_{\max}=400$, $Y_{\min}=0$, $X-Y=400$ gross, $300$ net of $W$. $404$ gross with Aces.
$100/50$: $Y_{\min}=150-200=-50$, $X-Y=450$ signed, $454$ with Aces. Net card+Tichu swing $=P_0+T_w-T_\ell-G_\ell=100+200+200-200=300$.

Strict $3\!-\!4$ per-player:
$X_{\max}=P_0+W+400=600$, $Y_{\min}=G_\ell-400$
$100/100$: $Y_{\min}=-200$, $X-Y=800$ signed, $804$ with Aces.
$100/50$: $X-Y=850$ signed, $854$ with Aces.

Realizability:
In real play the winning team must contain the first player to empty, so the formal $3\!-\!4$ reading is not realizable. Logical reading $\lnot(W_1\land W_2)$ i.e. the team does not occupy both first and second places allows the realizable order $W_1$ first, $L$ second, $W_2$ third, $L_1$ fourth with $p_w=P_0,p_\ell=0$.
Weak/loose reading $G_w=100$, $G_\ell=100$ on $100/100$, $G_w-G_\ell=0$, $G_w-G_\ell=50$ on $100/50$.
One call per team with usual $T_w=+200$, $T_\ell=-200$ per team:
commonly quoted $W$-first figure is $X=400$, $Y=-300$, $X-Y=700$ signed on $100/100$, $750$ signed on $100/50$.
Per player weak reading gives $X-Y=P_0+W+400+400+G_w-G_\ell=1000$ signed on $100/100$, $1050$ signed on $100/50$, $1004/1054$ with Aces.

Current round consensus: Colleagues 1,2,3,5 all present the strict $3\!-\!4$ ceiling $400$ gross/$300$ net, $450$ signed on $100/50$, and note the realizable $W$-first $700/750$ alternative. Colleague 4 explicitly advocates consolidating on the strict $450$ signed, $400$ gross reading and keeping $700/750$ as an alternative remark.

Unresolved for the problem statement: which out convention is intended $100/100$ vs $100/50$, one-call-per-team vs per-player Tichu counting, whether signed negative $Y$ is allowed in $X-Y$, and whether “does not go out first and second’’ is intended strictly as winner $3\!-\!4$ or merely $\lnot(W_1\land W_2)$. Textbook strict figure most often quoted is $400$ gross $=300$ net winner last, $450$ signed on the commercial $100/50$ book; physically realizable maximum under natural reading is $700$ signed one-call, $1000$ signed per-player, $750/1050$ on $100/50$.
